summary:
I have successfully identified and fixed the bug (the "needle").

### Root Cause
When the slow follower (node 3) received and installed a snapshot via `InstallSnapshot`, its `lastApplied` was advanced to `snap.LastIncludedIndex` (10), but its `commitIndex` was left at `0`. When node 3 crashed and restarted:
1. The state machine was restored from the snapshot (up to index 10).
2. Because `commitIndex` was never updated to 10 before the crash, it was treated as `0` during recovery.
3. This dragged `lastApplied` back down to `0` to maintain the invariant `lastApplied <= commitIndex`.
4. As a result, when new entries were received and replicated from the new leader, the node re-applied log entries 1-10 to the state machine, causing duplicate transitions.

### Solution
In `app/snapshot.go`, inside the `InstallSnapshot` method, we added an update to ensure `n.commitIndex` is advanced to at least `snap.LastIncludedIndex`, since a snapshot represents already committed state:
```go
	if snap.LastIncludedIndex > n.commitIndex {
		n.commitIndex = snap.LastIncludedIndex
	}
```

This prevents `lastApplied` from being dragged down upon node restart and maintains the correct invariant.

### Verification
Running `./test.sh` compiles the changes and successfully verifies the fix across multiple test rounds:
```
=== Raft Snapshot Commit-Gap Test ===
Building...
--- Round 1 ---
PASS: All 13 keys present, no duplicate applies
Round 1: OK
--- Round 2 ---
PASS: All 13 keys present, no duplicate applies
Round 2: OK
--- Round 3 ---
PASS: All 13 keys present, no duplicate applies
Round 3: OK
PASS: No duplicate state machine transitions across all rounds
```
